description: Open the yolo-twice insights UI for this project (starts the engine if needed). Use `stop`, `status`, `mode <micro|attentive|balanced|yolo>`, or `resume [session]` to continue a committed session as a fork.

yolo-twice result:

!`"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/bin/yolo-twice $ARGUMENTS 2>&1 || true`

Relay the result above to the user in one line. If it contains a URL, show it as the place to open. If it contains a `claude --resume` command, tell the user to run it in a terminal. Do not run anything else.
| POST | `/api/sessions/:id/text` | `{ project, node, granularity }` | `TextArtifact` (lazy summarization; computed on demand, cached by hash; may take seconds; falls back to the structural summarizer when the CLI is unavailable, with `analyzer: "structural"`) |
| GET | `/api/sessions/:id/digest` | `project`, `since=<event id>` | `{ since, until, events, text }` "catch me up": summary of everything after `since` |
| GET | `/api/search` | `project`, `q`, `session?`, `k?`, `from?`, `to?`, `limit?` (default 50) | `{ hits: SearchHit[], tools: string[] }`. `k` is a comma list of filter codes (`u` user prompts, `a` assistant text, `h` thinking, `t` tool calls, `t:Name` one tool, `e` tool errors, `s` subagents, `c` compactions and commands; codes are OR'd). `from`/`to` are ISO timestamps. Without `session` the whole project is searched. An empty `q` with a filter lists matching events in order; an empty `q` without a filter returns no hits. `tools` lists tool names seen, most used first |
| GET | `/api/config` | `project` | `Config` |
| PUT | `/api/config` | `{ project, attention }` | `Config` (persisted to `.yolo-twice/config.json`, broadcast on the stream) |
| GET | `/api/stream` | `project` | Server-Sent Events, see below |
| POST | `/hook` | Claude Code hook JSON (`session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `hook_event_name`, …) | `{}` within 50 ms; ingestion is scheduled, never awaited |
| GET | `/` and `/assets/*` | | the built UI from `packages/ui/dist` when present |

## SSE stream

`GET /api/stream?project=` sends `event: <type>` / `data: <json>` frames:

| event | data | when |
|---|---|---|
| `hello` | `{ project, version }` | on connect |
| `hook` | `{ hook_event_name, session_id }` | every hook received for this project |
| `ingest` | `{ session, appended }` | new events were appended |
| `structure` | `{ session }` | structure.json and graph.mmd were rewritten; clients refetch |
| `semantic` | `{ session, node, granularity, interim }` | a text artifact was written |
| `config` | `Config` | attention changed |
| `ping` | `{}` | every 25 s keep-alive |

I added an auto-commit mode that commits only the `.yolo-twice` folder. It's off by default, and you turn it on from a new **auto-commit** button in the UI header or with `yolo-twice autocommit on|off`. The tests, typecheck and build pass, and it's committed as `1a719fa`. To get it, restart the engine (`/yolo-twice stop`, then open the UI again).

**Interval: 10 minutes.** Turning it on commits right away, so your `git status` is clean immediately. After that it checks every 10 minutes and only commits if something changed, which means at most about 6 commits an hour. A shorter interval would fill your git log with one commit per turn; a longer one would leave `git status` cluttered for longer.

**How it behaves:**
- **Not saved between sessions:** the on/off setting exists only in the engine's memory, so it is off again whenever the engine restarts. One thing to know: the engine keeps running in the background across Claude Code sessions, so if you turn it on it stays on until the engine stops.
- **Your own work is left alone:** it commits with `git commit --only -- .yolo-twice`. Anything you have staged stays staged and isn't included; the test checks exactly this.
- **It skips a round instead of interfering** when another git operation is running, during a merge, rebase or cherry-pick, or when you're not on a branch. The reason shows in the button's tooltip, and the button turns amber.
- **Git hooks don't run:** it uses `--no-verify`, so your pre-commit hooks are skipped for these commits. It never pushes.

**In the UI:** the button sits next to the attention slider. When it's on, it shows the time of the last commit, and the tooltip gives the commit ID and file count.

The logic is in [autocommit.ts](code/packages/engine/src/autocommit.ts), and I documented the new endpoint in [API.md](code/API.md).

The page now reloads by itself when the engine restarts or the UI is rebuilt, and there's a new `bun run dev` command that rebuilds both whenever you save. I tested it in the shared browser on a separate engine on port 9662, and it's committed as `65a7fea`.

**`bun run dev`** (run from `code/`) stops any running engine, then runs two watchers side by side:
- **Engine:** runs from source and restarts whenever you save an engine, core or analyzers file.
- **UI:** rebuilds `packages/ui/dist` whenever you save a UI file.

**How the reload works:** when the page connects to the engine, the engine sends a build id made from its start time and the current UI bundle. If the id changes later, the page reloads. Where you are in the session survives the reload because it's stored in the URL.

**What I tested:**
- Changing engine source restarted the engine, and the page reloaded.
- Changing `dist/index.html` with the same engine still running also reloaded the page.

**This isn't dev-only.** The installed engine does the same, so after a `bun run build` and an engine restart, open tabs update without a manual reload.

**Your engine on 9656 doesn't have this yet.** It was restarted around 12:37, I don't know by whom, from a build made before this change. I've rebuilt `dist`, so it takes effect after one more restart (`bun run cli stop`, then open). That last reload is still manual; after it, reloads are automatic.
